artworks.title: Clytemnestra and Agamemnon
artworks.description: Guérin's Louvre night-scene: the returning king asleep as Clytemnestra hesitates with the dagger and Aegisthus urges the blow — Aeschylus' homecoming murder at the hinge.

artworks.title: Clytemnestra
artworks.description: Collier's queen just after the deed: bloodied axe in hand on the palace threshold — Agamemnon's murder already fact behind the curtain.

artworks.title: Clytemnestra from the Battlements of Argos Watches for the Beacon Fires Which Are to Announce the Return of Agamemnon
artworks.description: Leighton paints the watch that opens Aeschylus' Agamemnon: Clytemnestra alone on the Argive walls, waiting for the beacons that will bring her husband home to the axe.

artworks.title: The Ghost of Clytemnestra Awakening the Furies
artworks.description: Downman stages the sequel the murder demands: the queen's shade rouses the Erinyes against Orestes — blood calling for blood after Agamemnon's death.

films.title: Electra
films.description: The murder of Agamemnon hangs over Cacoyannis' Electra — the king already dead, his blood the debt his children will collect from Clytemnestra.

music.title: Elektra
music.description: Strauss and Hofmannsthal make the aftermath of Agamemnon's murder a nightmare of guilt — Elektra who will not let her mother's sleep rest.

popCulture.title: Agamemnon (play)
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: The first play of the Oresteia — Clytemnestra's axe in the bath still defines how tragedy stages a homecoming murder.

popCulture.title: Oresteia
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: The trilogy that begins with Agamemnon's death and ends in Athenian justice — Western drama's founding blood-cycle.

popCulture.title: Clytemnestra
popCulture.description: The queen who waits with the net and the blade — Agamemnon's murder forever wears her name.
